title: SPAN: a geometric model of effector tethering in R-loop genome editors
description:
SPAN bounds where a tethered deaminase can act on an R-loop, given linker statistics, steric exclusion and R-loop geometry alone. It is a geometric constraint on the reachable set rather than a per-nucleotide predictor. Three parameters are fitted to two published editing profiles and held fixed; all further predictions are made without adjustment, and are scored with each substrate position's deposited coordinate withheld.

The deposit contains the model, the analysis scripts that produce every reported number, the recorded results those scripts write, the container definition they run in, and a corpus of 50 published architectures drawn from seven publications, with linker lengths recorded in residues read from construct maps rather than by linker name, and a source register giving the status of every publication examined. Sampled conformational ensembles are not deposited: they are 20,000 linker chains and 8,000 substrate samples per entry and regenerate deterministically from the recorded seed using this code. Structural coordinates are not redistributed; data/fetch_structures.py retrieves them by accession from the Protein Data Bank.

Results: contour length does not move the predicted window across a sixteen-fold range, whereas attachment site does; across 185 buildable single-linker designs the predicted peak never falls outside protospacer positions 3 to 12 and lies within 5 to 11 across all sampling conditions, and the span, direction and rigidity a connector would need to reach the remaining positions are given; predicted window position agrees with measurement to within one nucleotide for most SpCas9-family architectures but does not improve on a constant predictor on this corpus; transfer to Cas12a fails by five to six nucleotides, with reach, capture radius, steric map, substrate treatment, fitted parameters and structural substitution eliminated in turn; and the displaced strand's path is not recoverable from linker statistics and steric exclusion, with a median error of 22.8 angstrom in SpCas9 at atomic resolution.
